titre_page: How to make your own blocks with functions? | Yop2D guide
description: Group nodes into a function, call it from any scene and add settings (inputs) to make your own blocks in Yop2D, without code.
h1: How to make your own blocks (functions)?
carte: Group nodes into a function and reuse it everywhere, with its own settings.
etapes: Resources → Functions → ＋, then open its Blueprint.
A start event, then the nodes you want.
The “Call function” node in a scene.
Inputs: a name, a type, a starting value.
blocs: A **function** is a small group of nodes that you give a name to. You build it once, then run it whenever you want with a single node, from any scene. It is your way of making **your own blocks**: you don't redo the same thing ten times and your Blueprints stay tidy.
a project open in the editor.
Open the **Resources** panel (on the left of the editor) and unfold the **Functions** part.
Tap **＋**, type a short name (for example `Give_points`) and confirm.
Tap your function's name to select it, then the button that opens its Blueprint (the icon of linked nodes).
A function is a file of your project: it is exported with your game and works in every scene.
You are in the function's Blueprint (the title says “Function: …”). Place the [[NoeudEventStart]] event: this is where the function starts.
Then connect the nodes you want. For this example: [[ajouter_variable]] (variable `score`), then [[toast]].
In a scene's Blueprint, add the [[appeler_fonction]] node.
Tap the **Function** line and choose your function.
When this node is reached, the function's nodes run, then the Blueprint carries on.
Be careful not to put [[appeler_fonction]] under [[NoeudEventChaqueImage]] by accident: the function would start again on every frame.
Without settings, a function always does the same thing. **Inputs** let you set it on every call: how many points, which message, what speed…
In the function's Blueprint, tap the **Function inputs** button (a sliders icon, in the top bar).
Tap **+ Add an input**. Give it a **name** (for example `points`), a **type** (Number, Text or Yes / no) and a **starting value** (for example 10). Confirm, then save with 💾.

Inside the function, use the input by writing `=points` in place of a number. For example, put `=points` in the value of [[ajouter_variable]]. For a message, put `=message` in the text setting of [[toast]].
Go back to the scene's Blueprint: the [[appeler_fonction]] node now shows one line per input. Change the value: 50 points here, 10 points elsewhere.

An input can also receive a calculation, for example `=score * 2`. If you leave the line as it is, the starting value is used. Inside the function, an input takes priority over a variable with the same name.
**“Function not found”:** it was renamed or deleted. Choose it again in [[appeler_fonction]].
**Nothing happens:** check that there is a [[NoeudEventStart]] event at the start of the function, and that you saved with 💾.
**The setting lines don't appear:** save the function with its inputs first, then reopen the [[appeler_fonction]] node.
**An input name is refused:** write it as one word (letters, digits and _), without spaces.
**A function that calls itself:** Yop2D stops after a few calls so the game doesn't freeze.
